about.title: Pasadena Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You're on the ground outside a storefront on Colorado Boulevard or in a parking structure near Fair Oaks Avenue, embarrassed, checking whether anything is broken. Only later, once the wrist is in a cast or the back won't loosen up, does the question surface: was that floor or walkway supposed to be like that? In California, property owners and the businesses occupying their buildings owe visitors reasonable care. That doesn't make them responsible for every stumble in Pasadena. It does mean that when an owner knew about a spill, a loose handrail, or a dark stairwell, or should have discovered it with ordinary attention, and did nothing to fix or flag it, the injured person may have a claim. Proving that notice is the heart of most premises cases in Los Angeles County. We handle these claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Pasadena Residents Choose Us After a Fall

items.title: We know how to prove notice
items.desc: California requires showing the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to fix or warn about it. Our team builds that case from inspection logs, prior complaints, and how long the condition existed.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most California premises claims carry a two-year filing deadline, but claims against a public entity, such as the City of Pasadena, move on a much shorter clock. Getting started early helps keep every option open.

items.title: Fast action on surveillance video
items.desc: Stores, garages, and apartment buildings often overwrite footage within days or weeks. We can send a preservation demand right away so the recording of your fall isn't lost.

items.question: I tripped on a broken sidewalk in Pasadena. Is that different from falling inside a store?
items.answer: It can be, because the sidewalk may be maintained by the City of Pasadena or another public agency rather than a private owner. Claims against a government entity in California must start with a formal claim filed on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years, sometimes only months after the injury. Photograph the exact spot, note the nearest address or cross street, and contact us promptly so the right party is identified in time.

items.question: The store says I wasn't watching where I was walking. Does that end my claim?
items.answer: Not under California law. The state uses pure comparative fault, which means your recovery is reduced by whatever percentage of blame is assigned to you rather than eliminated. If a spill sat on the floor without a cone or a mop for a long stretch, the owner's share of responsibility still matters even if you were looking at your phone.

items.question: What should I do in the first few days after a fall on someone else's property?
items.answer: Get medical care and keep every record, because gaps in treatment are often used against injured people. Photograph the hazard, your footwear, and the surrounding area, and write down the names of any witnesses or employees you spoke with. Ask the business in writing to preserve any camera footage, then reach out so our team can take over the evidence work while you focus on healing.
